title: SNR‑guided per‑cohort KV quantization evaluation (FP8 / INT8 / INT4)
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: Evaluate a signal‑to‑noise‑ratio (SNR) driven quantization policy for the KV cache that assigns per‑cohort compression formats (FP8, INT8, INT4) at write time to minimize GPU memory while bounding downstream quality regressions. Motivation: prior global quantization sweeps show good average savings but introduce high-tail regressions for some prompt cohorts; continuous batching and varying sequence lengths amplify those regressions under load. This ticket scopes experiments, evaluation metrics, and runtime fallback rules for deploying an SNR‑aware quantizer into the serving runtime.

Scope:
- Implement offline SNR estimator for KV vectors (per layer, per head) that can run over sampled eval logs.
- Build cohorting heuristics (prefix tokens, prompt length, model family) to group requests for per‑cohort quant decisions.
- Run controlled experiments for FP8/INT8/INT4 encodings gated by an SNR threshold to estimate quality tradeoffs across workloads.
- Measure GPU memory savings, per‑token latency impact (write + read), batch packing density, and quality metrics (perplexity drift, token‑level edit distance, downstream task accuracy).
- Produce runtime policy prototype: dynamic per‑cohort encoding with lightweight KV tagging, fallback to higher‑fidelity variants when regression observed or when prefix cache hits high.

This work aims to tie model‑level fidelity (SNR) to operational levers (format choice, batching behavior) so we can safely recover >30% KV memory in typical chat workloads while keeping customer‑visible regressions below our thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: SNR estimator implementation validated against float32 reference on sampled eval set (correlation > 0.88 with measured output delta)
Experiment runs completed for at least two model families (gpt-open-7B, gpt-open-70B) covering short-chat, long-context, and instruction prompts
Measured memory reduction and latency delta reported per workload; memory reduction >= 25% on aggregated chat workload without >2% regression in downstream task accuracy
Runtime prototype that annotates KV writes with encoding metadata and a simple fallback policy deployable behind a runtime flag
Experiment artifacts (notebooks, dashboards, PRs) linked in ticket and reviewed by Research/Applied ML and Serving teams
experiment_plan: Data selection: sample 100k cached requests from production demo tenants (anonymized) across three cohorts: short-chat (<64 tokens), medium (64-512), long (>512)
Instrumentation: add offline KV extractor that dumps layer/head vectors for a subset of requests to GCS with stable seed
SNR metric: compute per‑vector SNR = 20 * log10(||signal|| / ||signal - quant(signal)||) using layerwise float32 reference
Policy grid: evaluate thresholds for SNR cutpoints mapped to {FP8, INT8, INT4}; test both uniform per‑layer thresholds and adaptive per‑head thresholds
Quality tests: compare generated continuations (1000 prompts per cohort) against float32 baseline using BLEU-like token overlap, delta perplexity, and a small human‑labeled QA pass for edge cases
Runtime perf: simulate continuous batching by replaying traces at 1x, 5x, and 10x QPS to measure batching depth, KV cache hit patterns, and end‑to‑end latency
Failure modes: run stress scenarios where hot prefixes lead to high KV reuse and verify fallback triggers correctly when quality metrics deviate
results_summary:
(progress snapshot as of 2025‑11‑18)

1) SNR estimator: implemented and validated on synthetic vectors and a 10k request sample for gpt-open-7B. Correlation with measured token delta = 0.89 for layerwise median SNR; per‑head correlation varies (0.7–0.93). We observed that lower layers have consistently higher SNR tolerance for INT4.

2) Memory savings: initial offline quantization using per‑cohort mapping (SNR threshold tuned on medium cohort) yields 28% aggregate KV memory reduction. Savings are higher (~38%) for short‑chat cohort due to lower per‑request KV size overhead.

3) Quality: overall downstream task accuracy drop is 1.6% for the tuned FP8/INT8 mix; introducing INT4 for aggressive cohorts increased regression to 3.8% in the long‑context cohort. Token perplexity drift correlates strongly with SNR < 8dB.

4) Latency: encoding/decoding overhead adds 0.45ms per token on our CUDA kernels for INT8 path and 0.9ms for INT4 (due to dequant code path still in Python+CUDA kernel transition). Batch packing increased slightly (+3% tokens per batch) because quantized KV fits denser into GPU memory, enabling larger in‑flight batch sizes in the simulator at higher QPS.

5) Runtime prototype: KV tag metadata added to encoded cache entries. Fallback rule implemented: if a cohort experiences >2% increase in token‑level edit distance over a sliding window of 500 samples, mark cohort as "elevated" and re‑encode subsequent writes at higher fidelity for 10 minutes.

6) Observed risks: INT4 introduces brittle regressions for transformer layers interacting with rotary embeddings in the model variant we tested. We need layer‑aware exceptions for positional layers.
